title: Contact, Unclassified
summary: Only one Frame launches. The other five kids play ground roles simultaneously, in real danger, on the same clock. Cut between a level-12 initiative order and a level-1 one.
groundRoleRule: The other five kids play ground roles simultaneously, in real danger, on the same clock.
downtime: None. One continuous day — makes Day 2's sudden abundance of scheduling feel like a different game.

scenes.title: Ordinary Tuesday
scenes.description: All six kids, one mundane scene. Lightly press one Anchor per player. Nothing happens — this scene exists so scene 8 hurts.

scenes.title: The alert
scenes.description: Sirens, automated evacuation, a shape in the sky the public feeds have already stopped showing. The adults don't know what to do either.

scenes.title: Ground layer
scenes.description: Five level-1 kids navigate a collapsing arcology toward shelter. Three decision points, each costing time on a visible clock, each optionally helping someone else. Sets each kid's starting Resonance and confirms their Anchors through play rather than character-sheet fiat.

scenes.title: The summons
scenes.description: One kid is pulled to pilot — and was explicitly not the intended pilot. The Directorate's actual choice is unavailable, injured, or otherwise off the board. This kid is a contingency, not a chosen one.

scenes.title: The refusal
scenes.description: Let them say no, and mean it if they do. Cut back to the ground layer, mid-danger, and let that player watch the consequence play out among the other five characters — not an abstract city.

scenes.title: The plug
scenes.description: Slow this down. The first harmonics number is read aloud, flatly, by an adult who has done this before.

scenes.title: The fight
scenes.description: Three rounds, two actions, internal-power duration ticking down visibly. The Claimant is immune to damage until its interdiction field is broken; the field's weak point is only visible from ground level — the other five spot it and call it up, making the non-piloting players load-bearing inside a level-12 fight while they remain level 1. Round three: Bleed hits 10. GM takes the sheet. The Frame wins. Don't describe it from the cockpit.

scenes.title: The cost
scenes.description: Immediately — not next session. Something the ground five spent the whole episode protecting is gone, specifically because of how the fight was won.

scenes.title: Debrief
scenes.description: A sterile room. The ratio read out loud as a bare number. Then the second gut-punch: the other five learn their own Frames were assigned weeks ago. Nobody told them.

castingNote: Hand the pilot role to your most rules-fluent player; they're best placed to improvise inside a system they don't yet fully control.

firstPilotSpecialRules.advantage: Starts at 68% Resonance (Harmonised, three actions from round one). In-fiction, this is dissociation reading as high sync, not talent — something is wrong, and that's why it works.
firstPilotSpecialRules.disadvantage: A real injury from the opening impairs ground scenes, and they permanently lose one discretionary slice per day to ongoing medical obligations.
firstPilotSpecialRules.decay: Their 68% was bought with Bleed and decays toward baseline over time. They'll spend the opening arc chasing a number they got for free exactly once.
